title: Degraded Request Orbit Visualizer — interactive timeline for retries and payload deltas
creator: Anna Park
description: Design and prototype a compact, interactive visualizer (codenamed 'Orbit') to help engineers triage degraded requests. The Orbit visualizer arranges a failed request at the center and places retries, fallback model calls, and downstream partner requests as concentric lanes. Each orbit node encodes status, duration, and error class; hovering opens a payload snapshot diff. Purpose: reduce time-to-root-cause for production incidents by surfacing retry chains, payload drift, and error taxonomy in a single glance.
acceptance_criteria: Clickable timeline that shows primary request + all retries and fallback calls in concentric lanes
Hovering a node reveals payload snapshot with before/after diff and KV cache indicators
Nodes are colored by error taxonomy and include tooltips for SLO breach risk and observed latency
Filters for time range, model/version, route, and customer ID applied to the Orbit view
Quick actions: open payload inspector, create incident (links to incident tracker), copy raw payload, and request reprocess
Prototype performance: initial load for 50 related events <= 1.2s in staging telemetry dataset
design_notes: Key interaction patterns: 1) radial layout where distance from center indicates chronological order (inner = earlier), 2) stroke thickness encodes request duration, 3) small badge for retry count and cache hits. We prioritize dense packing for compact consoles but include a temporal scrubber to expand a focused time window. Payload diffs show only altered top-level keys by default, with 'expand full payload' to avoid cognitive overload and PII exposure. Accessibility: ensure colorblind-safe palette and keyboard navigation for nodes and actions.
decisions: 1) Use radial timeline instead of linear waterfall to better show repeated retries without horizontal scrolling. 2) Default payload diffs to top-level keys only; deep diffs require explicit expand to mitigate accidental exposure of sensitive fields. 3) Map error taxonomy to four stable buckets (Network, ModelError, RateLimit/Quota, Validation) for clarity and filter performance.
tradeoffs: Radial layout improves density but is less familiar than waterfall; mitigating with inline legends and an onboarding tooltip. Showing full payloads increases context but risks loading times and PII; mitigated via sampling and server-side redaction flags. Real-time streaming of live retries complicates stable rendering — we will snapshot the chain at query time and surface a 'live tail' toggle.
review_feedback: PM (Jin Patel): add an action to link Orbit nodes directly to a runbook and incident template
Eng (Priya Nair): backend needs an API that returns precomputed diffs and an ID for streaming; recommend adding payload size cap of 200KB for inline diffs
SRE (Carlos Vega): surface KV cache TTL and whether a memoized response was returned for the node when available
Design (Lina Chow): reduce visual noise by collapsing repeat identical retries into a stacked micro-node with a count badge
Privacy (Maya Singh): require explicit 'redaction-consent' flag from backend before showing any unredacted payload fields
usability_findings: Rapid testing with 6 backend engineers: median time to ID root cause reduced from 4m10s (waterfall baseline) to 2m05s using Orbit. Main friction: first-time users misinterpreted lane distances as severity, clarified in onboarding copy. Users appreciate payload diff preview and incident quick actions. Two testers requested grouping by downstream service instead of strict chronology.
implementation_notes: Backend API must provide: chain-id, ordered events with timestamps, precomputed top-level diffs, error_taxonomy label, cache_hit boolean, payload_redaction_flag, and small preview payload. Frontend should virtualize node render for chains >200 nodes. Add instrumentation events for node_expand, action_incident_create, and payload_copy.
